sanskrit: dhruvo 'si dharuṇo 'stṛto viśvakarmaṇā sudhṛtaḥ | mā tvā samudra ud vadhīn mā suparṇo 'vyathamāna imaṃ dṛṃha ||
english: You are firm, you are a support, unassailed, well-held by Viśvakarman. May the ocean not uproot you; may the eagle not—unshaken one, strengthen this.

sanskrit: āṣāḍho 'si sahamānaḥ sahasva- -ārātiṃ sahasva pṛtanāyataḥ | sahasravīryo 'si sa imaṃ jinva ||
english: You are unconquered, you are overpowering; overpower the enemy, overpower the one who marshals troops. You are of a thousand-fold heroic strength—with that, quicken this one.

sanskrit: adbhyaḥ saṃbhūto 'si pṛthivyā rasāc ca viśvakarmaṇaḥ samavartathā adhi | tasya tvaṣṭā vidadhad eti rūpaṃ vidvān tat te devam ājānam agre ||
english: You came into being from the waters and from the essence of the earth; you arose above Viśvakarman. Tvaṣṭṛ proceeds, assigning your form; knowing that divine origin of yours, he was first.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭiś cādhvaryo navatiś ca pāśā hotāram agnim antarā vicṛttāḥ | sinanti pākam ati dhīra ety ṛtasya panthām anv eti vidvān ||
english: Sixty and ninety snares are spread between the Adhvaryu-priest and Agni the Hotṛ. They ensnare the simple man; the wise one passes beyond, and follows the path of cosmic order.

sanskrit: yo adhvaryuḥ sapta hotrāṇi vidvān pūrvo hotur yajata ājigharti | ūrdhvaṃ sa yajñam adhvaraṃ kṛṇoti ya īṃ ciketa haviṣo vibhāge ||
english: The Adhvaryu who, knowing the seven priestly offices, sacrifices in precedence of the Hotṛ and kindles the fire—he elevates the sacrifice and makes the offering non-violent; he who understands the distribution of the oblation.

sanskrit: atro vibhaktari haviṣo vibhāge mā nir bhākṣīd bhāginaṃ mopahaty | mo abhāgo vidita yo mumoha ||
english: Here, O distributor, in the distribution of the oblation, let him not exclude the one entitled to a share, let him not harm him. Let not one known as shareless be deluded.

sanskrit: vāta ā vātu bheṣajaṃ śambhu mayobhu no hṛde | pra ṇa āyūṃṣi tāriṣat ||
english: May the wind blow the healing herb, the auspicious and bliss-bringing one, to our heart. May it carry our life-spans across to safety.

sanskrit: uta vāta pitāsi na uta bhrātota naḥ sakhā | sa no jīvātave kṛdhi ||
english: O Wind, you are our father, you are our brother, and you are our friend. Make us to live.

sanskrit: yad ado vāta te gṛhe nihitaṃ bheṣajaṃ guhā | tasya no dehi jīvase ||
english: Whatever healing remedy is stored in secret in your house up there, O Wind—give us of that to live.

sanskrit: yo na jīvo 'si na mṛto devānām amṛtagarbho 'si svapna | varuṇaṇī te mātā yamaḥ pitā ||
english: O Dream, you are neither living nor dead among the gods; you carry immortality within you. Varuṇānī is your mother, Yama is your father.

sanskrit: yathā kalāṃ yathā śaphaṃ yatha rṇaṃ saṃnayanti | evāha duṣvapnyaṃ sarvam apriye saṃ nayāmasi ||
english: As they settle a fraction, as they settle a hoof-debt, as they settle a debt—so do we today settle all evil dreaming into the inauspicious one.

sanskrit: ararur nāmāsi taṃ tvā svapna tathā vidma sa naḥ svapna susvapnyatāṃ dhehi ||
english: You are called Araru—thus do we know you, O Dream. O Dream, establish good dreaming for us.

sanskrit: naitasyāgre havir adanti devā nirbhakta eṣa sukṛtasya lokāt | pāpīṃ dhiyaṃ jujuṣa ātmanaiṣa sa hi duṣkṛn manuṣyeṣv antaḥ ||
english: The gods do not eat the oblation of this one before all others; he is excluded from the world of the well-doers. He himself has cultivated an evil mind—for he is a malefactor dwelling among humans.

sanskrit: yo mātṛhā pitṛhā svasṛhā ye ca duṣkṛtaḥ | vidhiṣau te amṛkṣata malaṃ manuṣyā iva ||
english: He who has slain his mother, slain his father, slain his sister, and those other evildoers—their defilement was wiped off on the two prescribed ones, as men wipe off filth.

sanskrit: etad evaitaṃ nirarṣur devā bhrūṇaghnyā lokam apy ety eṣaḥ | na te cṛtye haviṣā nāthitasya rāṣṭram ete śakrā vi cṛtanti pāśam ||
english: This very one the gods drove out—the slayer of the embryo reaches that world. Not for your ritual act with oblation does one who is implored receive a kingdom; these mighty ones sever the snare.

sanskrit: ya ākho yo vyukho vīṇavām̐ iha sarpati | taṃ pari paribheṣajaṃ vṛścikajambhanam asi ||
english: That serpent which glides here as the ākhū, as the vyūkha, making a rustling sound—against it you are the encircling medicine, the crusher of scorpions.

sanskrit: mayūro atti vṛścikaṃ mayūraṃ vayam admasi | taṃ pari paribheṣajaṃ vṛścikajambhanam asi ||
english: The peacock eats the scorpion; we eat the peacock. Against it you are the encircling medicine, the crusher of scorpions.

sanskrit: āpa id vā u bheṣajīr āpo amīvacātanīḥ | āpo viśvasya bheṣajīr āpo vṛścikajambhanīḥ ||
english: The waters are indeed the healers; the waters drive away disease. The waters are the healer of everything; the waters crush the scorpion.

sanskrit: tvam agne vratapā asi deva ā martyeṣv ā | tvaṃ yajñeṣv īḍyaḥ ||
english: You, O Agni, are the guardian of vows, O god, both among the immortals and among mortals. You are to be praised at the sacrifices.

sanskrit: yad vo vayaṃ pramināma vratāni viduṣāṃ devā aviduṣṭarāsaḥ | agniṣ ṭad viśvād ā pṛṇātu vidvān somasya yo brāhmaṇām̐ āviveśa ||
english: Whatever vows of yours we have transgressed, O gods—we who know less than those who know—may Agni, the all-knowing one who has entered into the Soma and the Brāhmaṇas, make that whole again.

sanskrit: ā devānām api panthām aganma yac chaknavāma tad anu pravodhum | agnir vidvān sa yajāt sa id dhotā so adhvaraṃ sa ṛtūn kalpayāti ||
english: We have come upon the path of the gods; whatever we are able to convey along it—may Agni the all-knowing one sacrifice; he alone is the Hotṛ; he conducts the offering and appoints the seasonal rites.

sanskrit: ut tudā i śimidvatīṃ vi duryoṇā iva dupadā i | ud asyāḥ pātayā manaḥ śaśvatībhyaḥ samābhyaḥ ||
english: Rouse up the possessive woman, drive her away like one with a bad dwelling, like one with a bad foot. Fly her mind away from the everlasting seasons.

sanskrit: pakvaṃ māṃsam ivāsinā śakuniprapatanāṃ kṛdhi | mṛgām̐ anu pra pātaya marīcīr anu nāśaya ||
english: Make her fly away like cooked meat before a sword, like a bird in flight. Make the deer fly away in pursuit; destroy her mirage-desires.

sanskrit: viṣvañcau gāvāv ā kuru viṣvañcau yugyā uta | utāsau sūrya ūrdhvaṃ viṣvañcau vāṃ vy ā karat ||
english: Turn the two cows in opposite directions; turn the two yoked ones in opposite directions. May yonder sun on high turn the two of you asunder in opposite directions.

sanskrit: viṣam ugraṃ viṣaṃ sthiraṃ viṣasya mahimā mahān | viṣaṃ parasvataḥ śiraḥ śatadhā vy apātayat ||
english: Violent is the poison, firm is the poison, great is the greatness of the poison. The poison made the enemy's head fly apart into a hundred pieces.

sanskrit: saṃ daha vrajaṃ yathā vasudhā vasu vartayat | yaṃ viṣa prasarpasi sam agnir iva taṃ daha ||
english: Burn them together as a cattle-pen, as the earth rolls forth its wealth. Whomever you creep into, O poison, burn him up as fire does.

sanskrit: gṛhāṇa māṃsāny ava lomāni pātaya | pāṃśūn kṛkāṭa ā vāpāc chindhy uttānapādam ardaya ||
english: Seize hold of the flesh, shake off the body-hairs. Sow dust into the vertebrae; cut them apart; torment the one who lies with feet upward.

sanskrit: madhor ahaṃ madhutaro madhughān madhumattaraḥ | āsani kila me madhu mukhe nimandanaṃ kṛtam ||
english: I am sweeter than honey, sweeter than the honey-pourer, more full of sweetness. Honey in my mouth indeed—a sweet abode has been made there.

sanskrit: mām it tvam abhi cākaśo mṛgas tṛṣyann ivodakam | adhaspadān ma ud vadān maṇḍūko gośaphād iva ||
english: You gaze upon me alone, like a deer thirsting for water. Speak up to me from beneath my feet, like a frog from a cow's hoof-print.

sanskrit: ud vadā me adhaspadān maṇḍūko gośaphād iva | atho 'pa cakrā āsāsai śvā bandha ivāhataḥ ||
english: Speak up to me from beneath my feet, like a frog from a cow's hoof-print. And then, to sit and wait yonder—like a bound dog that has been struck.

sanskrit: ā vada bahulaṃ goṣṭhaṃ suvīraṃ bahupūruṣam | yatheto na pramīyātā evā me goṣṭham ā vada ||
english: Proclaim a plentiful cow-pen, rich in good heroes, rich in many men—so that from here they may not perish. Thus proclaim my cow-pen.

sanskrit: ā vada duhituṣ pate bhrātur jāmātar ā vada | paścā ta udbhūtaḥ sphigaḥ kiṣkindhānām avīr jahi ||
english: Proclaim, O lord of the daughter; proclaim, O brother-in-law. The buttocks of those without heroes have risen up behind you—slay the kiṣkindhā folk.

sanskrit: yad ulūko vadati mogham etad yat kapotaḥ padam agnau kṛṇoti | śrutakarṇāya kavaye stomyāya tasmai yamāya namo astv adya ||
english: When the owl calls out, that is futile; when the dove makes a step in the fire—to that Yama who has listened with attentive ears, the poet, the praiseworthy one, let there be homage today.

sanskrit: ya aindrāḥ pāśā ye ca vāruṇā āre asmat tān devī nirṛtir dadhātu ||
english: The snares that belong to Indra and those that belong to Varuṇa—may the goddess Nirṛti place them far from us.

sanskrit: ye vaiśvānarāḥ pāśā ye ca mārutā āre asmat tān devī nirṛtir dadhātu ||
english: The snares that belong to Vaiśvānara and those that belong to the Maruts—may the goddess Nirṛti place them far from us.

sanskrit: ye vaiśvadevāḥ pāśā ye ca vaiśvakarmaṇā āre asmat tān devī nirṛtir dadhātu ||
english: The snares that belong to the Viśvedevas and those that belong to Viśvakarman—may the goddess Nirṛti place them far from us.

sanskrit: nārade kitave varuṇe soma aicchan mahimānaṃ mahāntam | avindat taṃ viśvakarmā samudre akṣāṇāṃ klandam ainam asmin dadhāmi ||
english: Among Nārada, the gambler, Varuṇa, and Soma, they sought the great majesty. Viśvakarman found it in the ocean; I place the weeping of dice into this one.

sanskrit: yad dhastayor yac cakṣuṣor mano yat praviveśa te | skandān asya praskandena klandena klandayāmi tat ||
english: Whatever mind has entered into your hands and into your eyes—with a springing motion, with the weeping-curse I make that weep in his joints.

sanskrit: tisro devīr apsarasa ākaikā sākaikā pretaprayām ety ekasyā nāma | juṣāṇā apsarasa ājyasya sahaso vyantu svāhā ||
english: Three divine Apsarases—one by one, each alone, each going on the path of the departed—the name of one of them is told. May the Apsarases, enjoying the clarified butter, go forth together mightily—svāhā.

sanskrit: atyākṣaṃ tvā manasā- -atyākṣaṃ hṛdayena tvā | atyākṣaṃ sarvair aṅgais tvā tathā hi tyajanaṃ kṛtam ||
english: I have overcome you with the mind; I have overcome you with the heart. I have overcome you with all my limbs—for thus the abandonment-spell has been performed.

sanskrit: imā yāḥ prati nandatha striyaḥ pumāṃsam anvitam | sarvāḥ saṃgatya brūta tejane tyajanaṃ kṛtam ||
english: You women who rejoice to greet the man who pursues you—all of you, gather together and declare: in the sharpening-rite, the abandonment has been performed.

sanskrit: tyajanaṃ me dyāvāpṛthivī adhātāṃ tyajanaṃ devaḥ savitā bṛhaspatiḥ | agniś ca tubhyaṃ sūryaś ca tejane tyajanaṃ kṛtam ||
english: Heaven and Earth have established abandonment for me; the god Savitṛ and Bṛhaspati have established abandonment. And Agni and Sūrya—in the sharpening-rite, the abandonment has been performed for you.

sanskrit: saṃ divaḥ saṃ pṛthivyāḥ saṃ vātāt saṃ nadībhyaḥ | saṃskandam indra ābharat sa āgāt so 'gād idam ||
english: From the sky, from the earth, from the wind, from the rivers—Indra brought the saṃskanda plant together. It came here; it has come to this place.

sanskrit: saṃskandam oja ojasā devebhir nāma te hitam | hiraṇyanāma nāma te saṃskandāsy oṣadhe ||
english: Saṃskanda-strength, with its strength—the name has been assigned to you by the gods. Your name is golden-name; you are the Saṃskanda herb.

sanskrit: saṃ samudro nadībhiḥ saṃ dyāvāpṛthivī ubhe | saṃ jāyā patyā yonyāṃ saṃskandāsy oṣadhe ||
english: The ocean is united with the rivers; both heaven and earth are united. Wife and husband are united in the womb—you are the Saṃskanda herb.

sanskrit: saṃ te śīrṣṇaḥ kapālāni saṃ yoniṃ saṃgavīnyau | saṃ te sarvāṇy aṅgāni saṃ skandenābhi dadhmasi ||
english: We breathe together the skull-plates of your head, we breathe together the womb, the two saṃgavinī veins. We breathe all your limbs together—we breathe them together through the Skanda-herb.

sanskrit: śriyaṃ dhātur mayi dhehi śriyā mādhipatiṃ kṛṇu | viśām īśāno maghavān indro mā yaśasā nayat ||
english: O Dhātṛ, establish splendor in me; through splendor make me a lord. May Indra, the bountiful one who rules over the people, lead me with fame.

sanskrit: mayi tyad indriyaṃ bṛhan mayi dakṣa uta kratuḥ | gharmas triś cid vi bhātu mā gāyatrīcchandasā virāḍjyotiṣā tasya doham aśīya ||
english: May that great Indra-power reside in me, and skill and resolve in me. May the hot-milk vessel shine forth three times in me; may I win the milk of it—of the Gāyatrī meter, of the Virāj-light.

sanskrit: arkāsadhasthau kavimātariśvānau yamāṅgirasaḥ | yaśasvinaṃ mā devā yaśasaḥ kṛṇuta svāhā ||
english: The two who dwell in the Arka plant's abode, the two poets Mātariśvan—Yama and the Aṅgirases: may the gods make me glorious, possessed of fame—svāhā.
